definitions.explanation: The hot, sharp, or pungent taste sensation produced by ingredients like chili peppers, wasabi, ginger, and pepper. One of the basic taste components in Japanese cuisine.

examples.japanese: わさびの{辛味|からみ}が{鼻|はな}に{抜|ぬ}ける。
examples.english: The spiciness of the wasabi hits the nose.

examples.japanese: この{料理|りょうり}は{辛味|からみ}が{強|つよ}すぎて{食|た}べられない。
examples.english: This dish is too spicy for me to eat.

examples.japanese: {唐辛子|とうがらし}の{辛味|からみ}と{味噌|みそ}の{甘|あま}さがうまく{調和|ちょうわ}して、{深|ふか}い{味|あじ}わいになっている。
examples.english: The spiciness of the chili pepper and the sweetness of the miso harmonize well, creating a deep flavor.

notes:
Derived from the adjective {辛|から}い (spicy, hot) with the suffix ～み indicating a quality or degree of that taste.

Japanese distinguishes between different types of {辛味|からみ}: the burning heat of {唐辛子|とうがらし} (chili pepper), the sharp nasal punch of わさび (wasabi), the warmth of {生姜|しょうが} (ginger), and the bite of {胡椒|こしょう} (pepper).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {辛味|からみ}が{強|つよ}い (strongly spicy)
- {辛味|からみ}を{加|くわ}える (to add spiciness)
- {辛味|からみ}を{抑|おさ}える (to tone down the spiciness)
- {辛味|からみ}{調味料|ちょうみりょう} (spicy condiment)
- {辛味|からみ}{大根|だいこん} (spicy daikon radish)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {辛|から}さ: spiciness (emphasizes degree; {辛味|からみ} emphasizes the quality of the flavor itself)
- {甘味|あまみ}: sweetness (parallel construction for a different taste)
